comparison: Both strongly support the finding that tLTD requires presynaptic NMDARs (C9, C40-C43). Peer review additionally includes C107 (genetic evidence localizing NMDARs presynaptically). All reviewers explicitly affirm this conclusion with high confidence.

Both strongly support the non-ionotropic NMDAR signaling mechanism (C10-C11, C44-C51). Peer review additionally includes C54-C55 (frequency independence conclusions). Editor and reviewers describe findings as 'compelling' and explicitly affirm the non-ionotropic mechanism.

Perfect alignment on 7-CK experiments (C15-C16, C52-C53). Both evaluations support the complementary pharmacological evidence for non-ionotropic signaling. No concerns raised by peer reviewers about these specific experiments.

Complete agreement on JNK2 requirement and RIM1αβ independence (C12-C13, C59-C68). Both evaluations emphasize the strong genetic and pharmacological evidence. Peer review specifically notes the dissociation from RIM1αβ as an accepted finding.

Strong alignment on JGRi1 peptide experiments demonstrating presynaptic JNK2/STX1a requirement (C14, C69-C79). OpenEval includes C73 which peer review does not explicitly mention, but both affirm the presynaptic localization and JNK2/STX1a interaction findings.

Both support the main conclusions (C17, C39, C80-C82) with peer review additionally including C104-C106, C142-C143. Peer reviewers describe these as 'fundamental findings' that 'elegantly address a long-standing conundrum.' OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple lines of evidence.

OpenEval R7 focuses on mechanistic interpretation (C104-C107) explaining frequency independence. Peer R6 includes these claims (C104-C106) as part of broader main conclusions. Both evaluations support the logic connecting non-ionotropic signaling to frequency independence.

Both support the novelty claims about JNK2's role in tLTD (C118, C120-C121). Peer review implicitly accepts novelty through enthusiastic endorsement. OpenEval additionally includes C142 (general principle suggestion), which peer R7 does not explicitly address.
Perfect alignment on age limitation acknowledgment (C140-C141). Both evaluations support the appropriateness of this caveat. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the limitation through lack of criticism.

Complete agreement on methodological approaches (C146-C147, C150-C152). Peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'highly sophisticated and technically challenging' methods and 'thorough' experiments. Both evaluations strongly support the experimental design.
